items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: The transcript mentions Jerome Kern only in a footnote as the composer of 'Yesterdays'; the interviewee discusses performing the song but does not mention any personal interaction or relationship with Kern.

ctx.x: Ahh, let's see. I think it was "Oo Bop Sha Bam" and then I did "Body and Soul", naturally, and then "Manteca" and then I did "Yesterdays" which John Lewis wrote*, he was in the band too, you know. He went later with the Modern Jazz Quartet. That was my feature in the band, yeah. And of course when "Manteca" came out on R.C.A. Victor that was his biggest hit. That did a lot for Dizzy and it did a lot for me, you know. I had sixteen bars and
*possibly an arrangement; Jerome Kern composed "Yesterdays" in 1933; lyrics by Otto Harbach.

everybody liked it, you know. But I was broken hearted because Dizzy was pushin' and the manager Milt Buckner...Milt Shaw...was pushin for me to do "Yes-terdays", but Charlie Ventura had already done it and they didn't go for it, you know. But that really got to me.
